$comment: Optics by gun (tools/content/optics.mjs; docs/GUNPLAY_SPEC.md §15, "Optics by gun"; owner, 2026-11-18: red dot or holographic for close range, 2-3x for rifles and carbines, a full scope for snipers, each with its own reticle). `kinds`: what an optic is: its reticle, its housing (`none`: the gun's own iron sights; `tube` and `frame`: built in code on the gun's top, client game/opticHousing.ts; `magtube`: a magnifying tube built there, looked through like the model's own tube (client game/opticView.ts), its zoom the kind's `power` over the hip view; `model`: the model's own scope tube, the weapon's `view.optic`; `overlay`: the full-screen scope, the weapon's `view.zoomFov`), and its aimed field of view: `adsFov` (a share of the hip's, the 1x sights) or `mag` (the range of magnification over the hip view the kind covers; each weapon's own zoom stays in its weapon file and must lie inside it). `glass` (metres at scale 1): how high the window's middle stands over the mount, its half width and height, the housing's length, and its foot's (`foot`, default the length: the flat stretch of the gun's top it needs). `reticle` sizes are tangents of the angle at the eye. `weapons`: per hand-held gun the optic it carries (`default`) and those it may carry (`allowed`: those a player may pick for it in their loadout, Profile → Favourite loadout → Optics, docs/GUNPLAY_SPEC.md §15 "Optic choice"; every built housing in it stands on one mount, found for the first of them), `hasSight` (owner, 2026-11-27, "two sights stacked": a gun shows its own sight or an added one, never both): what the model has of its own, read off it on the sight sheet (`__sights.inspect`): `"optic"` (a scope, red dot or holographic sight, or a sight box: it aims down that, irons or a `window` in it, and no housing is built on it, the tool refuses one), `"irons"` (iron sights only: a housing built in code may stand on its top, seated) or false (no sights); with an optional `mount` ({ at: [x, y, z], scale, reason }) where the measured mount point is wrong, or a `window` ({ at, half: [w, h], round?, lens?, reason }) where the model has an open sight of its own to look through (no housing is built: the glass and its mark go in the model's window, at `at`, the middle of the opening on the eye's side of everything in it; while aimed the window is a clip: nothing of the gun behind the opening is drawn, so scraps of a model inside its sight box never show in the sight picture; `round`: a round eyepiece, the glass and its clip a disc of the half height; `lens`: the z range [from, to] of a closed sight's own glass and body, hidden by the clip, which the check along the barrel leaves out). `none`: hand-held guns that keep the aim they had (the gun's top under the eye, the HUD's aim dot), each with its reason. Mounted guns, melee weapons and tools need no entry. `steps` (a magnified kind, or one weapon): the zoom steps the mouse wheel moves through while scoped, each a share of the weapon's own aimed field of view; the first is always 1 (the zoom the gun comes up at), the rest get smaller (0.45: the field of view at 45 %, about 2.2 times closer). `feel`: scope feel for every magnified optic (docs/GUNPLAY_SPEC.md §15, "Scope feel"; the client's game/scopeFeel.ts): `sway` the drift's size (radians of real aim), `swayHeld` and `swaySpent` its multiples while holding breath (Shift) and while out of breath, `settle` the seconds its size takes to ease between them, `breathSeconds` how long a full breath holds, `recoverSeconds` how long an empty one takes to refill, `readyAt` how full it must be after running out before it can be held again. Run `node tools/content/optics.mjs` after a change.
